Although its powers are poorly understood, I have every faith it will prove to be vital to the completion of our mission.|Jackson Farseeker|<ref name="RPG" />}}
'''Jackson Farseeker''' was the grandfather of [[Jill Farseeker]], and a retired [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Captain/Legends|captain]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Farseeker and his granddaughter traveled with her father, [[Roark Garnet/Legends|Roark Garnet]], aboard his [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] ''[[Dorion Discus]]''.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Could be trouble, young Garnet.|Jackson Farseeker|<ref name="RPG" />}}
Jackson Farseeker was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], reaching the [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] of [[Captain/Legends|captain]] before retiring. At some point, he sired a [[Jackson Farseeker's daughter|daughter]], who bore him a granddaughter, [[Jill Farseeker|Jill]], after a relationship with the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Roark Garnet/Legends|Roark Garnet]]. Sometime during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Farseeker and Jill met Garnet, who had had little contact with his daughter, and were traveling aboard his [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]], the ''[[Dorion Discus]]'', with him and the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Tantos Dree]]. While leaving the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Thorgeld I]], the ''Dorion Discus'' was hailed by the [[Imperial Customs Frigate]] [[Assessor (Imperial Customs Frigate)|''Assessor'']], requesting they heave to for a customs inspection. Dree made it clear that the Empire could not discover his presence aboard, forcing Garnet to first attempt to bluff the ''Assessor'' into letting them go, then initiating evasive maneuvers when they did not believe him. Farseeker spent the time [[Astrogation/Legends|plotting]] a jump to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] to allow the ''Dorion Discus'' to escape. After the two [[Starship/Legends|ships]] traded fire, Farseeker successfully plotted the course, allowing the ship to jump to [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]].<ref name="RPG" />

Sometime later, an individual named [[Farsten]] attempted to bargain with Farseeker to acquire the mysterious [[Alien/Legends|alien]] device called [[Ou'tranoi/Legends|''ou'tranoi'']], offering 100 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] for it. Farseeker refused to sell it at any price, believing that the device would be instrumental in the success of their mission. Later, Farseeker met a [[Unidentified tentacled alien|tentacled alien]] in a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] and left in their company. Seven [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] later, Roark Garnet entered the cantina looking for him. Garnet paid the aliens a number of credits to jog their memory about what happened when they encountered Farseeker.<ref name="RPG" />

==Personality and traits==
Despite serving the Empire during his life, Jackson Farseeker was not loyal to the institution by the time of the Galactic Civil War, openly consorting with smugglers and bounty hunters, and willingly disobeying Imperial customs edicts. He came across as pompous but fatherly, and was a able to plot courses to navigate ships through hyperspace.<ref name="RPG" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Sorry, Jackson. Your bargain skill is only 2D. He's got you outclassed.''"<br />"''Stuff and nonsense! Jackson is ''my'' character, and I'm not giving him the ''ou'tranoi''.|The gamemaster and Jackson Farseeker's player|<ref name="RPG" />}}
Jackson Farseeker appeared in several example scenarios in [[1987]]'s [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']], published by [[West End Games]].<ref name="RPG" />
